hotspots.title: Javier Milei’s re-election bid and economic defense
hotspots.blurb: Javier Milei confirmed his 2027 re-election bid, defending his economic policies amid criticism over rising loan defaults, inflation, and poverty. His aggressive rhetoric against journalists and political opponents has intensified, framing the election as a battle between progress and decadence.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to Milei’s polarizing leadership style, which blends triumphant self-assurance with combative grievance politics, amplifying affective investment among supporters and detractors alike.

hotspots.title: Lega’s internal rebellion against Salvini’s leadership
hotspots.blurb: Matteo Salvini faces growing dissent within the Lega party, with northern governors and regional leaders demanding greater autonomy and a shift away from his centralized leadership. The rebellion threatens to fracture the party ahead of key regional elections and the 2027 national vote.
hotspots.affect: The internal strife is charged with high affective investment due to Salvini’s perceived betrayal of the party’s northern roots, fueling moral outrage and existential fears about the Lega’s future.

hotspots.title: AfD’s rise and far-right governance threats in Germany
hotspots.blurb: The Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) leads polls in Saxony-Anhalt and other eastern German states, with its far-right platform gaining traction amid fears of extremism. The party’s potential governance raises alarms about democratic backsliding, anti-immigration policies, and EU relations.
hotspots.affect: This hotspot is defined by intense affective investment due to alarmist framing of the AfD as a threat to democracy, cross-source repetition of extremism accusations, and moral panic over potential governance.
